title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Strata and common-area cleaning
audience: Owners and account managers of strata and common-area cleaning businesses who quote weekly or fortnightly work for owners corporations, strata committees and their managers.
learningOutcomes: Write a common-area offer with a clear promised standard, visit window, time frame and conditions
Identify the friction and risk an owners corporation or strata committee carries, and reduce them
Price the offer on value and cost, not only on time

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer
instruction.body: 'We clean the common areas' is a service. 'We clean the foyer, stairs, corridors, lift, bin room and car park entry every week to a written checklist, send the manager a photo log each visit, and return within two working days for any item a lot owner reports' is an offer. The committee buys a standard it can check, and a supplier that will not need chasing.

instruction.heading: The five parts of an offer
instruction.body: A clear outcome, such as common areas in a stated condition by 8 am on cleaning day; a defined visit window that avoids residents' peak times; the work the committee must do, such as providing fob or key access, bin-room access and water and power; the certainty you provide, such as a checklist, a photo log and a monthly report; and the risk you carry, such as the return visit. Keep each part specific and checkable. Put the scope and exclusions in writing, because a written quote can become binding once it is accepted (business.gov.au, 'Prepare quotes', last updated 1 August 2025).

instruction.heading: Reducing friction
instruction.body: Make access, the sign-off step and the reporting simple. One named contact for the manager, one monthly report and one fob or key process reduce the decisions the committee has to make. Clients often accept a higher price for fewer interruptions, because they are paying for reliability and a clear record.

instruction.heading: Guarantees and claims
instruction.body: A guarantee must be something you can deliver and afford. Consumer guarantees under the Australian Consumer Law apply to services, and a 'no refunds' line does not override a customer's rights for services. A written workmanship warranty is an optional extra that sits on top of those guarantees (business.gov.au, 'Warranties and refunds', last updated 27 May 2025). Consumer Victoria explains that a service provider gets a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault free of charge (last updated 13 October 2023), but that page sets no fix window, so write your own. Do not publish a measured claim, such as a percentage of common areas passing an inspection, unless you can show the inspection record. Check current ACCC guidance before publishing any measurable claim.

instruction.heading: Pricing on value
instruction.body: Price from the scope and the risk, then check against your cost and visit time. A committee often compares several quotes, and Bugden Allen, writing about Victoria, says multiple quotes are best practice rather than a requirement of the Owners Corporations Act 2006 (published 3 October 2025, updated 24 July 2026). Make your offer comparable by stating the standard, frequency, exclusions and one clear total, and say whether GST is included (ACCC, last modified 15 July 2026). Vendor guidance gives common areas at $1.80 to $3.00 per square metre per clean, and mid-rise residential buildings at $800 to $2,500 a month (Clean Group, updated 15 March 2026). These two figures do not reconcile with each other, so do not use either one in a quote until its basis is confirmed. A stepped package, with a weekly clean, a fortnightly deep clean and a quarterly report, can show the committee what each level adds (Jobber Academy, published May 2021, updated 8 October 2024).

procedure: Write the outcome in one sentence a committee member would repeat.
Set a visit window that avoids residents' peak times, and record how often you meet it.
List what the committee must provide, such as access and water, and reduce each step.
Add one certainty element: a checklist, a photo log or a monthly report.
Decide the return-visit promise and check that you can staff it within the time you state.
Price from scope and cost, then check the rate against the vendor ranges and the basis of each.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner quotes a weekly price for a 24-lot building and loses to a lower quote. The strata manager says the committee wants to compare like with like, and that the lower quote does not show what is included.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Rewrite the offer so the committee can compare it, and state the price basis you can support.
workedExamples.reasoning: A written offer that states the checklist, the photo log, the monthly report, the return-visit promise, the exclusions and one total with GST status lets the committee compare like with like. The price should come from your own hours and cost. The vendor's common-area range of $1.80 to $3.00 per square metre per clean and its mid-rise range of $800 to $2,500 a month do not reconcile with each other (Clean Group, updated 15 March 2026), so neither is used as the basis. Confirm the basis of any vendor figure before it goes in a quote.

commonErrors.error: Making a return-visit promise you cannot afford to honour
commonErrors.prevention: Limit the promise to something you control, such as a return visit within two working days, and write the time into the offer.

commonErrors.error: Stating a result you cannot substantiate
commonErrors.prevention: Use only results you have measured and can show, such as inspection records, and keep the records.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. In Victoria, owners corporation rules are set by the Owners Corporations Act 2006; in NSW, strata committee rules are set by the Strata Schemes Management Act 2015. This lesson does not state either Act's quote or contract rules, and it does not grant any licence. Check the rules for your state before acting.

qualityStandard: Offer and pricing decisions are written down, and each offer states the basis of its price.
documentationEvidence: Written offer with the checklist, photo-log commitment, exclusions and the price basis, and the decision made.
summary: A strata offer promises a checkable standard, a set visit window and a return-visit promise, and it is compared with other quotes.
Price from your own cost and the scope. Do not use the vendor's per-square-metre and monthly figures together until their basis is confirmed.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of a strata offer does the owners corporation buy?
What should a return-visit promise be?
options: Impossible to claim on in any case
Only for new customers and friends
Something you can deliver and afford

officialReferences.covers: Taken from the research file (team4-R-sol03-tactics, tactic 11): misleading statements about price are prohibited, which supports showing one all-in price with GST status. The page was not re-read for this variant. Publisher: ACCC.

sourceReferences: business.gov.au, 'Prepare quotes', https://business.gov.au/people/contractors/prepare-quotes, last updated 1 August 2025. Supports: a written quote becomes binding once accepted.

Consumer Victoria, 'Services not done with due care and skill', https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/products-and-services/problem-with-a-service/services-not-done-with-due-care-and-skill, last updated 13 October 2023. Supports: a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault free of charge. The page sets no fix-window length.

Bugden Allen (Julia Moroz), via LookUpStrata, 'Vic Q&A: our OC engages preferred contractors without quotes or proper certification', https://www.lookupstrata.com.au/vic-qa-our-oc-engages-preferred-contractors-without-quotes-or-proper-certification/, published 3 October 2025, updated 24 July 2026. Secondary commentary; check the Act. Supports: multiple quotes are best practice, not a Victorian Act requirement.

Clean Group, 'Commercial cleaning pricing guide', https://www.clean-group.com.au/how-much-does-workplace-cleaning-cost-in-australia, updated 15 March 2026. Vendor source. Supports: strata common areas at $1.80 to $3.00 per square metre per clean; mid-rise residential at $800 to $2,500 a month. These two figures do not reconcile.
